problem: Existing spatial-reasoning benchmarks for VLLMs are mostly passive and static, set in household scenes with QA over images or videos. They test isolated skills and lack dynamic obstacles, collision or safety metrics, and joint local-global planning.
motivation: Industrial settings such as warehouses have moving forklifts, robots and workers, and safety matters there. It is unclear how well VLLMs perform active, holistic spatial reasoning (perception, planning, action) in such dynamic environments, so the paper builds a benchmark with a zero-shot pipeline and safety metrics to expose this.
key_idea: A Unity-based benchmark of 12 dynamic warehouses with a zero-shot PointGoal pipeline (egocentric image + global odometry + action-state memory) and new collision and warning ratio metrics for evaluating VLLM spatial reasoning and safety.
insight: Even the best VLLM (Claude-Sonnet-4.6) reaches only 79.17% SR versus 100% for humans, and all models have high collision and warning ratios, so planning, active exploration and distance estimation remain weak. Ablations show dynamics lower SR and raise warnings, and action-state memory helps (Claude-Sonnet-4.5 collision ratio 54.76% -> 27.68%). Adding a top-down map generally hurts, since it distracts the model (Gemini-2.5-flash CR 32.14% -> 41.23%), and memory length 5 beats 3 and 10.
method: Warehouse scenarios: 12 high-fidelity Unity HDRP warehouses built manually by 5 experts, with racks, forklifts, robots and workers; dynamic objects and workers follow hand-designed spline trajectories, and hand-crafted colliders provide collision detection.

Sensors and headless mode: two 1024x1024 egocentric RGB-D cameras, a fixed bird's-eye camera tracking a red cone for the agent's pixel position, and a cross-platform headless mode with a teleportation API.

Zero-shot PointGoal pipeline: the VLLM receives the egocentric image, its own and the target coordinates, heading, distance to target, a heading-direction mapping, and an action-state mapping prompt; it outputs JSON with reasoning and action from {forward, turn left, turn right, stop} (turns fixed at 90°, step 34 px).
Action-state memory: the last k=10 steps (position, theta, action, distance, target) are fed back to help detect loops and repeated failures.
Task-success and efficiency metrics: SR (final distance <= 20 px), DR (fraction of initial distance closed), AS (average steps per run).
Safety metrics: Collision Ratio (forward actions whose position does not change / total forward actions) and Warning Ratio (fraction of steps where the minimum depth in a forward ROI is below 1 m).
Protocol: 4 random start-target pairs per scene (48 runs), 70 steps each, 14 VLLMs via OpenRouter plus a human-expert baseline.

setting.backbone: 14 VLLMs evaluated zero-shot (10 closed-source: GPT-4o, GPT-5-mini, GPT-5.2, Claude-Haiku/Sonnet-4.5, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, Gemini-2.5-flash, Gemini-3-flash, Qwen3.5-plus, Seed-2.0-mini; 4 open-source: Qwen3-VL-8B/30B-A3B, LLaMA-4-Scout, Nemotron-nano-12B-v2-VL)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (depth used only for warning metric) + global odometry (agent pixel position, heading, target coordinates, distance) + action-state history
setting.action_space: discrete: forward (34 px), turn left/right (90°), stop
setting.privileged: ground-truth odometry (agent position, heading, target coordinates and distance) is given at every step

numbers.eval_set_note: 12 warehouses x 4 start-target pairs (48 runs), 70 steps each
numbers.extra: GT odometry provided; success threshold 20 px; 70-step budget

numbers_note: Table 1 has all 14 models; only the best closed model, GPT-5.2 and the best open model are listed here. Ablation results are mostly in figures, with a few values in the text.
results: On IndustryNav, Claude-Sonnet-4.6 is best with 79.17% SR and 89.26% DR, far below the human 100% SR, and closed-source models generally beat open-source ones (e.g. Qwen3-VL-8B 4.86% SR). Nemotron-nano-12B (55.56% SR) is the strongest open-source model. Every model has high collision (16-38%) and warning ratios, versus 17.97% CR and 8.4% WR for humans.
limitations: Sequential execution: the environment is static between steps, and the frame rate is limited by asset-dense scenes with no ray tracing.
Simplified discrete actions (90° turns, fixed step), only indoor warehouses, limited animation types, and small scale (48 runs per model, one run per model).
